decisions.quote: We conducted a replication of the eight choosing versus rejection problems in Shaﬁr (1993). We successfully replicated the results of Problem 4 and Problem 5 of the original study. However, in Problems 7 and 8 we found eﬀects in the direction opposite to the original ﬁndings and our ﬁndings for Problems 1, 2, 3, and 6 indicated support for the null hypothesis.
decisions.reason: The paper re-tests all eight problems (Experiments 1–8) from Shafir (1993) and explicitly reports that two successfully replicated, four supported the null, and two showed opposite effects, which is coded as mixed under the codebook rules for multiple tested findings from the same original paper that come out differently.

decisions.quote: We tested the competing theoretical assertion by Wedell (1997). Our results in support of this account suggest that the stimuli from the 1990s are still of relevance, at least for testing that account.
decisions.reason: Shafir (1993) is the sole target article of the replication; Wedell (1997) is cited for a competing theoretical account (the accentuation hypothesis) and analytical procedure applied as an extension to the Shafir (1993) stimuli, rather than as an empirical finding being replicated.

parent_objection: Only settle missing target1 Wedell1997 (Shafir outcome mixed remains settled). First reply excludes Wedell as theoretical account not empirical finding. Source explicitly says We tested the competing theoretical assertion by Wedell1997; follows Wedell1997 approach to calculate overall enriched-option preference and reports binary logistic mixed-effects regression supporting its accentuation hypothesis. Determine whether these are actually re-tested earlier published findings (conceptual replication and omitted target under paper-level enumeration) or theory-only application/extension to Shafir stimuli. Do not exclude solely because account is competing or theory-based; equally, citing or supporting a theory alone does not prove an empirical replication target. Inspect introduction, analysis, discussion, reference and supplied blind target for actual scope. Unsupported scope stays undeterminable; no invented empirical claims about unseen original.

shipped.title_o: Choosing versus rejecting: Why some options are both better and worse than others
shipped.outcome_quote: In a preregistered very close replication of the original study (N = 1026), we found no consistent support for the hypotheses across the eight problems: two had similar effects, two had opposite effects, and four showed no effects (overall d = −0.01 [−0.06,0.03]).
